review_note: COVID-19 had materially changed 2020 trading, management expected market contraction, acted to protect liquidity and disclosed scenarios involving covenant breach and additional funding; strategic cost reduction and internal restructuring added intervention evidence. Against that, 2019 EBITA margin improved to 8.1%, operating profit rose 50%, net debt fell £56m and leverage improved to 2.8x, supplying strong but temporally qualified contrary evidence.

Supply-chain and inflation pressure persisted, but pricing protected margins and the fixed-cost restructuring announced in 2020 had been completed and is excluded as a future target event. Adjusted EBITDA margin recovered above 32%, adjusted operating cash flow reached £76m, net debt fell £30m to 0.4x EBITDA and a healthy order book supplied multiple exceptional quantified offsets.

A 21% revenue decline in materially weaker residential markets led to decisive capacity and cost action, site rationalisation and closures, sales-team restructuring and a £30.8m exceptional restructuring charge. Adjusted operating profit and cash conversion fell, with conversion at 47% and net debt rising from £46m to £101m; 1.1x leverage, pricing discipline and stated readiness for recovery supplied limited contrary evidence. The disclosed 2023 programme is excluded as a future target event.

Cyclical market headwinds, organic revenue and profit declines, £52m of restructuring charges and a continuing £75m multi-year rationalisation programme indicated substantial intervention pressure. Adjusted margin nevertheless improved 20bps, operating cash flow rose 35% and restructuring savings were ahead of plan, supplying strong quantified offsets. The announced rationalisation and planned 2020 actions are excluded as future target events.

The platform reorganisation and complexity-reduction programme were strategic actions already disclosed and are excluded as future target events; no material unresolved Group pressure remained. Revenue rose 7%, adjusted operating profit 13%, adjusted margin 90bps, operating cash flow 26%, cash conversion reached 89% and a record Process Automation order book supplied multiple exceptional quantified offsets.

No specific unresolved operating or intervention pressure was evident. Adjusted operating profit rose 18%, adjusted margin increased 220bps to 21.1%, cash conversion reached 110%, statutory net debt remained only £0.3m after a £12.4m acquisition and the order book remained robust, supplying multiple exceptional quantified contrary indicators.
